completed_stage_receipts.summary: Classified the signal as a systemic execution-control defect: maintenance can be entered yet still be executed as a remembered checklist rather than a gated SOP.
Separated ingress reliability from post-entry execution reliability and classified the defect as post-hoc verification without sufficient pre-action control.
Mapped ingress, controller, state, mutation authorization, closure verifier, bootstrap, harness, persistence, resume and cleanup surfaces before further implementation.
Bound the issue to the recurring class where policy and reflection exist but operational execution can still bypass or post-hoc reconstruct required maintenance work.
Reused already distilled incident-learning evidence; the new fact is execution enforcement, not another need for more reminder prose.
Found an existing canonical maintenance controller and rejected a second SOP implementation; duplicate maintenance_sop.py and its tests were deleted.
Rejected more recall reminders and another supervisor agent; accepted strengthening the existing deterministic controller and attacked investigate, skip, reopen, checkpoint and closure paths.
Verified that controller execution and meta closure are separate and identified durable controller state plus closure binding as the remaining internal work; no user decision is required.
Kept account routing thin: cheap triage only at ingress, while detailed SOP remains repository-owned by policy/controller.
Chose one existing controller, one task-local durable state, and the existing meta verifier; no new agent, root policy, registry or parallel SOP.
Deletion test removed the duplicate maintenance_sop mechanism. Remaining payoff is to make prepatch durability and controller-complete closure mechanically required.
